key_insight: PC-GNO learns the full mid-plane six-component stress tensor field in concrete penetration by coupling graph neural operators with physics-informed message passing.
engineering_relevance: It enables field-level surrogate prediction for penetration-resistant concrete design, so engineers can derive stress criteria and energy indicators from one model instead of separate scalar surrogates.
method: Aggregate-resolved FEM generates 359 training cases at 100, 135, and 165 m/s for concrete strengths of 14, 23, and 48 MPa.
Message passing strength is tied to material impedance contrast across interfaces to encode physics of heterogeneous concrete.
Spectral normalization stabilizes the operator learning and constrains the update process.
evidence_signal: On single-step prediction, PC-GNO reports 80.16% mean accuracy across three levels, outperforming the preceding-frame baseline and achieving 87.9% with only 20,664 parameters.
watch_item: Performance is bounded by the training/evaluation regime and the studied impact velocities, strengths, and mesostructure distributions, so extrapolation beyond those conditions may be unreliable.
paper_title: A physics-coupled graph neural operator for mid-plane six-component stress tensor field prediction in concrete penetration
